name: GET /api/sla/alerts - List SLA escalation alerts
description: Returns the SLA alert ledger newest-first: who was notified, about which lead, at which escalation tier, and whether the notification actually landed. A read, so it answers 200. Every alert is a durable ROW, not just an outbound message - a manager escalation that exists only as a fired-and-forgotten notification cannot be audited, retried after a gateway outage, or shown in-app to somebody who missed the email. state tells the two apart: delivered means ProjexCloud sdk-notification accepted it, pending means the row exists and is visible in-app but the outbound send has not succeeded yet, so a gateway outage degrades the channel WITHOUT silencing the escalation. kind is the escalation tier: owner_warning goes to the lead's owner while the clock is still running (at_risk), and manager_breach goes to every active manager once the deadline has passed - notifying managers BEFORE a violation is the point, so the two tiers are separate rows with separate recipients. Filter by state, kind or lead_id; limit is clamped to 1..200 and defaults to 50. Alerts are raised by the monitoring sweep (POST /api/sla/evaluate), which is why this list can legitimately be EMPTY for a freshly captured lead - a lead inside its response window has nothing to escalate. Protected by the authenticate guard - the Authorization header is required on this GET, because an alert names who is late on which prospect. QA: depends on register, login, a captured lead and a sweep.

errorCases.when: state is present but not one of pending, delivered, acknowledged or failed; kind is present but not one of owner_warning or manager_breach; lead_id is present but not a well-formed UUID; or limit or offset is not a non-negative integer with limit at most 200
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
